title: A change to the Minimum Positive Participation threshold can never affect a poll already running
content:
A.1.12.2.6.1 makes the Minimum Positive Participation value itself amendable — "may be modified via a successful Governance Poll under the Operational Weekly Cycle" — and then immediately fences the amendment in time: "the new Minimum Positive Participation value will come into effect in the _following_ Monthly Governance Cycle. The Minimum Positive Participation value may not be changed for Ratification Polls that are in progress under any circumstances." The Action Tenet at A.1.12.2.6.1.0.4.1 defines "in progress" as a poll that has already started and where voting is taking place.

"Under any circumstances" is unusually absolute for the Atlas, and the reason is that a movable threshold is a retroactive veto. If the bar could be raised mid-vote, an amendment on track to pass could be defeated without a single additional No vote; lowered, a failing amendment could be rescued. Either move decides an outcome by changing the rules rather than the votes — and it would be available through the *lighter* weekly cycle, letting a three-day Poll overturn a two-week Ratification Poll's result.

The delay to the following cycle also removes the incentive to time such a change strategically. Anyone amending the threshold must do so blind to the specific proposals it will govern.

The generalizable rule: parameters of a decision procedure must be frozen at the moment the decision begins, or the procedure is only as strong as the discipline of whoever can edit it.
description: The value is amendable by an Operational Weekly Cycle Poll, but the new figure applies only from the following Monthly Cycle — the passing bar is fixed once voting opens.
